title: Functions on Graphs Review Test
description: Interpret representations, explain misconceptions, and transfer reasoning to unfamiliar cases.

questions.questionText: A plotted point on a function is (8, 12). What output belongs to this input?
questions.explanation: The horizontal coordinate 8 is the input. The vertical coordinate 12 is the output.

questions.questionText: A graph consists only of the points (0, 8), (1, 8), (2, 8). Is y a function of x?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes; each x has exactly one y.
questions.explanation: A horizontal set of points may share a height. No input has conflicting outputs.
options: No; repeated heights are forbidden.
No; functions must slope upward.
Yes; each x has exactly one y.
Yes; all point collections are functions.

questions.questionText: Two plotted points are (8, 1) and (8, 4). Why can no function of x contain both?
questions.correctAnswer: The vertical line x = 8 meets two different points.
questions.explanation: Different y-values only cause a conflict when their x-values agree. A vertical line holds the input fixed.
options: The points have different y-values.
The vertical line x = 8 meets two different points.
The graph must contain the origin.
A function can have only one point.

questions.questionText: The entire graph is the horizontal line y = 8. Does it pass the vertical-line test?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes; every vertical line meets it once.
questions.explanation: Use vertical, not horizontal, test lines. Each x gives the single output shown by the horizontal line.
options: No; a horizontal line meets it infinitely often.
No; its slope is zero.
Yes; it has no output.
Yes; every vertical line meets it once.

questions.questionText: The entire graph is the vertical line x = 8. Is it a function of x?
questions.correctAnswer: No; one x has many y-values.
questions.explanation: All points on a vertical line share one input while their outputs vary. Straightness alone does not establish a function.
options: Yes; it is a straight line.
Yes; x stays constant.
No; every straight line fails.
No; one x has many y-values.

questions.questionText: A plotted point on a function is (9, 13). What output belongs to this input?
questions.explanation: The horizontal coordinate 9 is the input. The vertical coordinate 13 is the output.

questions.questionText: A graph consists only of the points (0, 9), (1, 9), (2, 9). Is y a function of x?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes; each x has exactly one y.
questions.explanation: A horizontal set of points may share a height. No input has conflicting outputs.
options: No; repeated heights are forbidden.
Yes; each x has exactly one y.
No; functions must slope upward.
Yes; all point collections are functions.

questions.questionText: Two plotted points are (9, 1) and (9, 4). Why can no function of x contain both?
questions.correctAnswer: The vertical line x = 9 meets two different points.
questions.explanation: Different y-values only cause a conflict when their x-values agree. A vertical line holds the input fixed.
options: The vertical line x = 9 meets two different points.
The points have different y-values.
The graph must contain the origin.
A function can have only one point.

questions.questionText: A function graph is a straight line through (0, 8) and (2, 14). What is its output at x = 1?
questions.explanation: Halfway between x = 0 and x = 2, the height is halfway between 8 and 14: 11. The stated straight line justifies interpolation.

questions.questionText: A graph has only the three solid points (1, 8), (3, 9), (5, 10). Are inputs between these points included?
questions.correctAnswer: No; only inputs 1, 3, and 5 are shown as part of this graph.
questions.explanation: A discrete graph contains only its plotted points unless connecting segments or a larger rule are specified.
options: No; only inputs 1, 3, and 5 are shown as part of this graph.
Yes; automatically join every point.
Yes; all real inputs belong to every function.
No; isolated points cannot define a function.

questions.questionText: At x = 8, a graph has an open circle at y = 2 and a solid point at y = 5. Every other allowed x has one solid graph point. Does this graph define y as a function of x?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes; the open circle is excluded, leaving one output at that input.
questions.explanation: An open circle marks an excluded endpoint. Only the solid point supplies an output at this input.
options: No; open circles count as outputs.
No; one missing point invalidates every function.
Yes; the open circle is excluded, leaving one output at that input.
Yes; two included outputs would also be allowed.

questions.questionText: A curved graph turns at (8, 0). Every vertical line meets it at most once, but some horizontal lines meet it twice. Is y a function of x?
questions.explanation: A curve can assign one y per x. Horizontal repeats indicate shared outputs, which are allowed.
options: No; any horizontal repeat breaks a function.
Yes; the vertical-line test passes.
No; only straight graphs are functions.
Yes; every curve is a function.

questions.questionText: A line segment has solid endpoints (8, 3) and (12, 7). What is the greatest allowed input on this graph?
questions.explanation: Read the horizontal coordinates, not the heights. The right endpoint is included, so the greatest input is 12.

questions.questionText: A function graph is a straight line through (0, 9) and (2, 15). What is its output at x = 1?
questions.explanation: Halfway between x = 0 and x = 2, the height is halfway between 9 and 15: 12. The stated straight line justifies interpolation.
